note: A fixed copy of contracts/fields.json and its caseFiles declaration as hyper held them before http-forms took these cases (F-20 to F-27); the steps of the three servers read it until the servers call the core, and S-4 removes tests/legacy. Its sentences name the statements that point to the rules of http-forms.

fields.state: `fields` lists the values of `text` as `[name, values]` pairs in the order of their names, or is null when `text` fails with HY-42.

names.state: `names` lists the names of the values of `text` in the order of their first occurrence, or is null when `fields` is null.

fields.state: `fields` lists the form values of the body `body` of the type `type`, a text whose characters are its bytes, as `[name, values]` pairs, or is null when the body fails with HY-42.

files.state: `files` lists the files of the body in request order as objects with `name`, `filename`, `contentType` and `content`, where `content` is the text of the file and `contentType` is empty text for a part without a content type, or is null when `fields` is null.

stopped.state: `stopped` is true when the body `body`, a text whose characters are its bytes, given in chunks of `chunk` bytes, passed a limit, after which no chunk is given.

exceeded.state: `exceeded` is true when the body passed the body limit `limit`, the value limit `valueLimit`, the part limit `partLimit` or the file limit `fileLimit`.

held.state: `held` is the text of the bytes that the body holds as one value: empty text for a body that is read in chunks, which a multipart body of the type `type` is when `stream` is true, and for a body that passed the limit.

fields.state: `fields` lists the form values of the body as `[name, values]` pairs, read from the chunks or from the held bytes, or is null when the body failed or passed the limit.

files.state: `files` lists the files of the body in request order as objects with `name`, `filename`, `contentType`, `content`, the text of the bytes of the file, and `size`, or is null when `fields` is null.

entries.state: `entries` is the number of files in the directory of the body after its last chunk, or null for a body without a directory.

moved.state: `moved` is null when `move` is `none`, and else tells the move of the first file: for `new`, to a path that does not exist, and then a second time; for `exists`, to a path that exists; for `type`, to the number 7. `content` is the text of the bytes at the path after the first move, or of the file when the move failed; `left` is the number of files in the directory after it, or null without a directory; `again` is the message of the failure of the second move or of the failed move; `read` is the message of the failure of `content()` after the move, or null when the move failed; `class` is `value` for the class of HY-46.2 and `type` for TypeError.

removed.state: `removed` is true when the directory of the body does not exist after `remove()`, or null for a body without a directory.

file.state: `content` is a text whose characters U+0000 to U+00FF are bytes; `file` holds what `name()`, `filename()`, `contentType()`, `size()` and `content()` of `new UploadedFile(name, filename, contentType, bytes)` return, the content written as such a text.
